text: Why does a squared plus b squared equal c squared, for every right triangle?
Start with a big square, with sides a plus b long.
Place four copies of our triangle inside it, one in each corner.
The space left in the middle is a tilted square. Its side is c, so its area is c squared.
Now slide the same four triangles into new places, without changing them.
The space left is now two squares: one with side a, one with side b.
The big square and the four triangles never changed, so the empty space never changed either.
So c squared is exactly a squared plus b squared.
